title: Annotatio IV §.I: External obstacles — Devil’s instincts and arts; neither over-blame nor exempt him
pass_a_gloss: The former are comprehended under the various instincts, devices, and nefarious arts of the Devil, the first parent of lies, quarrels, and calumnies — so that they are neither to be exaggerated beyond measure with the common crowd accustomed to transfer nearly all its misdeeds and their blame onto the Devil, nor, with the Author of the fascinated World, to be exempted from the Community of human things or actions:
pass_b_english: The external sort fall under the Devil’s varied instincts, tricks, and wicked arts — he being the first parent of lies, quarrels, and slanders.
We must neither exaggerate with the crowd that dumps nearly every misdeed on the Devil, nor, with the author of this fascinated world, exempt him from the community of human things and deeds.
source_text: Priores variis Diaboli, mendaciorum, rixarum ac calumniarum parentis primi instinctibus, technis artibusque nefariis comprehenduntur, uti neutiquam cum vulgo, omnia propemodum malefacta sua horumque culpam in Diabolum transferre solito, supramodum exaggerandis, ita neque cum fascinati Mundi Autore vel rerum vel actionum humanarum Communitate eximendis:
notes: Devil as first parent of lies/quarrels; balance of blame.
